newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Lucas strong, Varity in soft patch.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Lucas strong, Varity in soft patch.

text.p: The two firms merging into LucasVarity Plc reported separate results on Tuesday that showed their differing resilience to weak global components markets.
John Grant, group finance director, said that the final full-year results from Lucas Industries showed the larger of the two engineers was "going into the merger in very good shape".
It produced a strong rise in pretax profits, up to 180.1 million stg from 135.8 million stg in the year-ago period.
U.S-based Varity, which issued summary second quarter data, showed flat operating profits as it hit short-term softness in automotive markets, Grant added.

While Grant stressed that he believed both sets of numbers were in line with market expectations, the sluggish growth in Varity's quarterly operating profit, which edged up to $52 million from $51 million, made its performance "OK, but not exciting", he said.
In its automotive sector, dominated by braking systems for light vehicles, Varity's operating profits rose to $30 million from $28 million while sales rose by 14 percent to $358 million.
Varity Perkins, specialising in diesel engines and with strong European exposure, saw sales slip to $259 million from $245 million and operating income ease a million to $22 million.
Grant said this slight fall partly reflected currency translation effects, compared with a year ago, as well as the weak truck and trailer market, especially in parts of Europe.

Unlike Varity's slowdown in the three months to the end of July, Lucas produced a set of 12-month figures up to the same date that showed it building strength, with firm organic growth and margin improvement.

Operating profits across the group, before exceptional items, rose by 35 percent while sales rose by 7.0 percent, while the group operating margin jumped 1.6 percentage points on productivity gains and helped by the elimination of lossmakers.

"On productivity, we've got some good numbers to report with sales per employee up 9.0 percent year on year," Grant told Reuters in a telephone interview. The increase in part reflects a two percent reduction in the workforce in the period.
Lucas had also pledged last year to work on improving its working capital efficiency and Grant said that the main gain had stemmed from lowering stocks "in a growing sales environment".
Sales growth from the Lucas automotive businesses was up 9.0 percent in the 12 months, in a market which he called "absolutely flat".
"That's a function of generally growing market share, and, in diesel, moving into higher value added, more sophisitcated systems," Grant said.
Lucas's aerospace division also reported an increase in sales, "for the first time in many years", as well as a profit margin recovery up to 8.9 percent, he added.
"Obviously the mood in the industry is now more buoyant. While we have a lot to do here, we feel we're well positioned."

Grant said the purchase 10 days ago of Boeing Georgia, from Boeing Co, had reinforced the message that LucasVarity will stick with aerospace -- a signal new chief executive Victor Rice has made clearly since the merger was announced this May.
